newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks to be rated higher in two years - Schroder.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks to be rated higher in two years - Schroder.

text.p: Hong Kong's stock market may be rated significantly higher within 18 months to two years as its risk premium is likely to keep falling in coming months, Schroder Investment Management (Hong Kong) Ltd said on Saturday.
"People in Hong Kong are taking a positive view of the change in sovereignty in 1997. This has led to a change in sentiment," David Lui, a director of the firm, told an investment seminar.
Britain hands the colony back to China on July 1.
Lui forecast the blue-chip Hang Seng Index, which reached a third consecutive record close on Friday at 13,856.40, will move between 12,000 and 15,500 during 1997.

"There is a positive correlation between Hong Kong's GDP (gross domestic product) and corporate earnings growth this year. As economic growth picks up to around 5.6 percent, corporate earnings are likely to increase by between 12 percent and 15 percent in 1997," he said.

Last November, the government estimated third-quarter GDP growth in 1996 at 5.0 to 5.5 percent year on year, against 3.3 and 4.3 percent in the first and second quarter respectively. It maintained its 1996 full-year growth forecast at 4.7 percent.
Lui predicted Asian stock markets in general are likely to provide a better return in 1997 than last year.
Given the modest valuation of many of the region's markets, they should provide a reasonable return over the next two years, he added.
Tino So, an assistant director of the firm, was also bullish about the prospects of Hong Kong stocks.

"The cyclical recovery of China's economy will lead to earnings growth among companies in both Hong Kong and China. Red chip stocks listed in Hong Kong will continue to be the main target for investment by institutional investors looking for a share of China's economic growth," she said.
Red chips are Hong Kong-listed companies with financial backing from China.
